canonical_dedup.result: No distinct source-proven POS outbox failure path identified. Existing findings cover generic worker fencing/retry and operational DLQ/alert visibility; adapter inability is already in INF-011. No severity/status changed and canonical ledger was not edited.

no_new_issue_observed: Payment recording queues a non-zero payment's invoice within its transaction; cycle IDs isolate re-collection after void.
Void and relay coordinate on the same causal lock; cancel only suppresses an invoice still PENDING and a later void event is queued in the same transaction.
Relay rechecks status after lock acquisition and records success or retry/dead state; existing mock tests cover the visible branches.

No real POS API adapter currently performs a vendor-side effect, so duplicate-on-lost-response behavior cannot be claimed from this snapshot. The port explicitly requires repeated references to be idempotent.
No DB/concurrency integration test was run; recommend vendor sandbox idempotency and PostgreSQL void-vs-relay acceptance when implementing an operational adapter.

limitations: Static source audit only; no tests, application runtime, database, VPS, provider, secrets or PHI access.
The snapshot export does not include the POS design document cited by repository inventory; conclusions use only files listed in this coverage record.
Mock tests do not prove PostgreSQL lock behavior or vendor idempotency; no actual delivery adapter exists to verify those contracts.
